subject: english
question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct voice.**

The journalist noted that the celebrity was having a very busy schedule that week.

options.text: The journalist noted, "The celebrity is having a very busy schedule this week."
The journalist said, "The celebrity was having a very busy schedule this week."
The journalist noted, "The celebrity has a busy schedule that week."
The journalist said, "The celebrity had a very busy schedule this week."

solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. "The journalist noted, 'The celebrity is having a very busy schedule this week.'".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The question requires converting the given indirect speech sentence into direct speech.
 
• The sentence provided in the question is: "*The journalist noted that the celebrity was having a very busy schedule that week.*"
 
• To convert indirect speech into direct speech, the following points must be considered:
 
 
• Identify the reporting verb ("noted" in this case).
 
• Change the tense of the reported clause. Since the reported speech uses "was having" (past continuous), it must be converted to "is having" (present continuous) in direct speech as per the context (that week → this week).
 
• Ensure the sentence structure aligns with direct speech rules (add quotation marks and correct pronoun usage).
 
 

Correct sentence: *The journalist noted, "The celebrity is having a very busy schedule this week."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rules for Indirect to Direct Speech Conversion:**
 
 
• Change the pronouns and time expressions as per the context.
 
• Adjust the tense according to the reporting verb (present or past tense).
 
• Enclose the direct speech in quotation marks.
 
 
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• Indirect: She said that she was reading a book. → Direct: She said, "I am reading a book."
 
• Indirect: He mentioned that he had completed the project. → Direct: He mentioned, "I have completed the project."
